entries.name: Analyze and visualize
entries.def: Find structure in data through representations of it: encode values as marks, link views, and interrogate what the encoding shows.

dims.name: Encoding choice
dims.q: How do values become visuals?

dims.name: View linkage
dims.q: How do multiple representations of the same data relate?

vars.name: Overview plus focus in one field

dims.name: Interrogation
dims.q: How does a person ask questions of the encoding?

vars.name: Write a query
vars.def: The question is posed by writing or editing text — SQL, PromQL, KQL, a pandas expression — and re-running it, rather than by acting on marks or controls; the primary interrogation in notebooks and in every observability explorer

dims.name: Analytical initiative
dims.q: Who drives the next analytical move?

vars.name: Fixed authored view
vars.def: Neither the person nor the system chooses the encoding during analysis: a designer or journalist fixed it beforehand and the reader only selects, filters within it and reads values — news graphics and every consumer analytics screen

entries.name: Chart
entries.def: A visual encoding of data values as marks and channels so a person can see distributions, comparisons and trends.

dims.name: Mark encoding
dims.q: What marks and channels carry the data?

vars.name: Animation
vars.def: A variable — almost always time — is mapped to motion over frames rather than to a static visual channel, with a play control and a scrubber; bar chart races, animated scatter trails

dims.name: Scale and axes
dims.q: How is the value space laid out?

dims.name: Mark interrogation
dims.q: How does a person inspect a mark?

dims.name: Encoding authorship
dims.q: Who chooses the encoding?

dims.name: Annotation and emphasis
dims.q: How are findings called out on the chart?

dims.name: Responsive encoding
dims.q: How does the chart change with space and density?

entries.name: Coordinated views
entries.def: Several views of the same or related data that stay synchronized through shared selection, filter or navigation.

dims.name: What is linked
dims.q: What state is shared across views?

dims.name: View arrangement
dims.q: How are the views placed?

vars.name: Overview–detail split
vars.def: One overview drives a detail view

dims.name: Coordination trigger
dims.q: What action propagates across views?

vars.name: Pan or zoom
vars.def: Moving the camera of one view (panning or zooming a map) re-queries the linked views

vars.name: Pan or zoom the view
vars.def: Moving or zooming one view is itself the coordinating action — the viewport becomes the query and the linked list, count or chart is recomputed for what is now in frame; the standard mechanism of map-plus-list products

dims.name: Selection scope
dims.q: What does a coordinating action apply to?

dims.name: Coordination feedback
dims.q: How does a person see what is linked?

dims.name: View authorship
dims.q: Who assembles and retunes the set of views?

entries.name: Focus + context
entries.def: A detailed focus region shown inside a continuously visible surrounding context in the same visual field—unlike overview–detail, which separates an overview of many items from a distinct detail view of one selected item.

dims.name: Focus–context relation
dims.q: How do focus and context share one field without becoming separate overview and detail views?

vars.name: Inset mini-map with live focus
vars.def: Small context map, large focus—still one navigational act

vars.name: Salience-only focus
vars.def: Focus is carved out by contrast rather than geometry — the attended region brightens or the rest dims while every element keeps its size and place; the XR and attention-aware case

dims.name: Spatial arrangement
dims.q: How are focus and context laid out in the field?

vars.name: Edge-aware focus panel
vars.def: Focus dominates; context as a strip

vars.name: Whole-field zoom
vars.def: There is no separate focus region: the entire viewport is the focus and the context is whatever remains visible around its edges, reached by zooming the one space; every zoomable map, canvas and globe works this way and none of the five arrangements describes it

vars.name: Whole-view zoom
vars.def: The entire viewport zooms in and out with no separate lens, inset or fisheye distortion — a plain zoomable map/canvas/graph

dims.name: Moving the focus
dims.q: How does the focus region move or resize?

dims.name: What densifies in focus
dims.q: What extra information appears inside the focus?

vars.name: Hidden context declutter
vars.def: Context shows less while focus shows more

dims.name: Degree of interest
dims.q: What determines what stays detailed versus compressed?

dims.name: Orientation feedback
dims.q: How does a person stay oriented while focused?

vars.name: Lost without leaving
vars.def: Must jump to a separate detail page

entries.name: Notebook
entries.def: An interleaved document of prose, code and outputs where analysis is authored as executable cells that produce tables, charts and narrative.

dims.name: Cell model
dims.q: What are cells and how do they relate?

dims.name: Execution flow
dims.q: In what order do cells run, and how is progress resumed?

dims.name: Output presentation
dims.q: What does a cell show after it runs?

dims.name: Authoring layout
dims.q: How are cells and side surfaces arranged?

dims.name: Runtime feedback
dims.q: How does the notebook report execution state?

dims.name: Assistance
dims.q: What does the environment contribute to the analysis?

entries.name: Pivot table
entries.def: A matrix that aggregates measures over chosen row and column dimensions, with drill, pivot and filter as first-class operations.

dims.name: Axis binding
dims.q: What fields sit on rows, columns and values?

dims.name: Aggregation
dims.q: How are cell values computed and shown?

dims.name: Drill and expand
dims.q: How does a person move between aggregate and detail?

dims.name: Layout density
dims.q: How is the matrix arranged on screen?

dims.name: Pivot authorship
dims.q: Who chooses the pivot configuration?

dims.name: Update lifecycle
dims.q: When do aggregates refresh?

entries.name: Browse collections
entries.def: Scan many comparable things, narrow to the relevant few, and focus on one — the activity behind shopping, inboxes, file systems and search results alike.

dims.name: Item representation
dims.q: How much of each item does the collection show, and in what abstracted form?

vars.name: Full inline
vars.def: The whole item in the collection

vars.name: Media only
vars.def: A thumbnail or artwork stands for the item with no text or attributes at all

vars.name: Visual encoding
vars.def: Position or colour stands for values

dims.name: Organization
dims.q: What structure holds the items, and how many collections are in play?

vars.name: Coordinated collections
vars.def: Several views of one set, linked

vars.name: Many collections
vars.def: One screen stacks several distinct, independently sourced collections (streaming shelves, store home rows) that are neither views of one set nor nested inside an item

dims.name: Arrangement
dims.q: How are items placed on the screen?

vars.name: Board
vars.def: Columns of cards by a value

vars.name: Shelves
vars.def: Stacked rows, each a horizontally scrolling strip for one group of items

vars.name: Graph
vars.def: Nodes and edges laid out by their links (force-directed), positions carrying no attribute value

dims.name: Narrowing and scale
dims.q: How does a person get from everything to the few that matter, and how much is present at once?

entries.name: Comparison table
entries.def: A few selected items side by side against shared attributes, so that differences can be read and a choice made.

dims.name: Criteria
dims.q: Which attributes become rows, and how are values shown?

vars.name: User-built criteria
vars.def: The person adds rows as they learn

dims.name: Item set
dims.q: Where do the compared items come from?

vars.name: Picked on the compare page
vars.def: The person chooses the items from a search box or dropdown on the comparison itself, over a third-party catalogue (not the vendor's own models, not result checkboxes)

vars.name: Gathered while browsing
vars.def: The person collects the items from wherever they were found — separate product pages across sites, clipped as they browse — rather than from one vendor's list, one results page's checkboxes, or a system suggestion

dims.name: Orientation
dims.q: Which way do items and criteria run?

dims.name: Difference emphasis
dims.q: How are differences made to stand out?

dims.name: Decision support
dims.q: Does the table help conclude, not only compare?

entries.name: Data table
entries.def: Items as rows against attributes as columns, built for scanning, comparing, sorting, filtering and acting on many items at once.

dims.name: Columns and cells
dims.q: Which attributes become columns, and how are values rendered?

vars.name: Generated columns
vars.def: A model extracts a column per row

dims.name: Density and structure
dims.q: How tightly are rows packed, what stays put, and how do rows expand?

vars.name: Detail row
vars.def: A panel opens under the row

dims.name: Selection and operations
dims.q: What can be selected, and what do operations apply to?

dims.name: Aggregation
dims.q: Are rows combined into groups or summaries?

vars.name: Footer aggregates
vars.def: Sum, average or count under a column

dims.name: Row detail
dims.q: How does one row open into its full record?

vars.name: Bottom panel
vars.def: The selected row's detail opens in a resizable panel docked below the whole table — the table stays complete above it, unlike a detail row that splits the rows apart or a side panel beside them

dims.name: Narrow screens
dims.q: What happens when there is no room for the columns?

entries.name: Feed
entries.def: An unbounded, continuously arriving stream of heterogeneous items, ordered by time or by ranking and consumed by scrolling.

dims.name: Post content
dims.q: How much of each post appears, and how uniform are the items?

vars.name: Injected modules
vars.def: Carousels of suggestions or stories inside the stream

dims.name: Ordering and sources
dims.q: Who decides what appears, and in what order?

vars.name: Ranked
vars.def: An algorithm orders by predicted interest

vars.name: Editorially curated
vars.def: People at the publisher choose and order the lead items; the feed is edited rather than ranked by predicted interest or sorted by the reader

vars.name: All posts
vars.def: Every submission on the platform, with no follow, topic or algorithmic selection

vars.name: Global pool
vars.def: Everything submitted to the site, identical for every visitor — no follows, no topic selection and no personalisation (Hacker News, a federated public timeline)

dims.name: Arrangement
dims.q: How is the stream laid out?

dims.name: Loading and position
dims.q: How does new content arrive, and does the feed remember where you were?

vars.name: New-posts pill
vars.def: New items wait behind a button

vars.name: Live insertion
vars.def: New items push into the stream as they arrive, moving the content under you, instead of waiting behind a pill or a refresh gesture

vars.name: Caught-up marker
vars.def: An explicit end of new items

vars.name: Resume position
vars.def: Returns to where you left off

dims.name: Nesting
dims.q: Do posts contain other posts?

vars.name: Clustered stories
vars.def: Several posts about one story grouped as a single unit under a lead item

vars.name: Clustered coverage
vars.def: One unit holds several independent posts about the same subject from different sources — a lead story with related coverage under it — which is neither a reply thread nor a repost of one post inside another

entries.name: File manager
entries.def: Browse, organize, preview and act on files and folders arranged in a hierarchy of locations.

dims.name: Item view
dims.q: How are files shown, and where does a preview appear?

vars.name: Viewer page
vars.def: Opens a viewer over the drive

dims.name: Navigation structure
dims.q: How are locations traversed, and how many are open at once?

dims.name: Metadata
dims.q: What does each file show about itself?

vars.name: Last change
vars.def: The last commit or change message shown per file or folder

dims.name: Grouping
dims.q: Are files grouped, and can a folder be a query?

dims.name: Shared ownership
dims.q: How are other people’s files and activity shown?

entries.name: Kanban board
entries.def: Items as cards in columns that stand for states or categories; moving a card between columns changes its value.

dims.name: Grouping
dims.q: What do columns and swimlanes stand for?

vars.name: By query
vars.def: Each lane is a saved filter

vars.name: Manual lanes
vars.def: Free-named lanes the team defines (e.g. Expedite) into which cards are placed by hand, not derived from a field

dims.name: Card and column content
dims.q: What does each card and column say about its items?

vars.name: Amount or value
vars.def: A monetary or numeric value on the card that is the point of the board — deal size, contract value — distinct from an effort Estimate; columnSummary already names its total but cardFields has no way to say the card carries it

dims.name: Transitions
dims.q: What happens when a card moves?

vars.name: Required fields
vars.def: A screen collects data on transition

dims.name: Card size and columns
dims.q: How are cards and columns sized and arranged?

vars.name: One at a time
vars.def: Only one column fills the screen at a time; swiping left or right moves to the adjacent column, e.g. Trello's mobile board

dims.name: Card detail
dims.q: Where does a card open?

dims.name: Board scope
dims.q: Which cards are on the board?

entries.name: Overview–detail
entries.def: An overview of many items, each shown through a few key attributes, paired with a detail view that shows many or all attributes of a selected item.

dims.name: Content
dims.q: Is information shown in the overview, the detail view or both, and how are overview attributes abstracted from detail attributes?

vars.name: In overview only
vars.def: An attribute that exists only as an overview representation

vars.name: In detail view only
vars.def: Present only once the item is opened

vars.name: In both views
vars.def: Repeated in overview and detail, interactive elements included

vars.name: Summary
vars.def: A generated précis of the detail

vars.name: Category
vars.def: A label standing for the detail

dims.name: Composition
dims.q: How are multiple overviews and detail views connected?

vars.name: One-to-one
vars.def: One overview opens one kind of detail view

vars.name: Many overviews to one detail view
vars.def: Several overviews of the same items or scopes

vars.name: One overview to many detail views
vars.def: Different detail views opened from one overview

vars.name: Overview inside detail view
vars.def: A detail view contains another overview

vars.name: Detail views in between
vars.def: An intermediate detail view opens a fuller one

vars.name: Independent
vars.def: Overviews do not react to each other

vars.name: Synchronized navigation
vars.def: Selecting in one overview navigates the other

dims.name: Layout
dims.q: How are overviews and detail views arranged, how are items organized, and how many details are open?

vars.name: Replace
vars.def: Detail swaps into the overview’s place

vars.name: Tooltip
vars.def: On hover or click, small and transient

vars.name: Side menu
vars.def: Overview as a menu beside the detail

dims.name: Invocation
dims.q: What opens a detail view, from which part of the item, and how does a person get back?

vars.name: Back button
vars.def: Returns from a replacing or floating detail

vars.name: Whole item
vars.def: The entire item view is the target

vars.name: Several attributes, several details
vars.def: Each attribute opens its own detail

dims.name: Scope of attributes
dims.q: Do attributes describe one item, or the whole collection?

vars.name: Per item
vars.def: Each item carries its own values

vars.name: Per collection
vars.def: Aggregates across items in the overview

entries.name: Accordion
entries.def: Stacked sections whose headers expand to reveal their content in place.

dims.name: Expansion policy
dims.q: How many sections can be open?

dims.name: Header content
dims.q: What does a closed section say about what is inside?

dims.name: Toggle
dims.q: How is a section opened?

dims.name: Memory
dims.q: Does it remember what was open?

entries.name: Bulk actions
entries.def: Selecting many items and applying one action to all of them.

dims.name: Selection model
dims.q: How are many items selected?

vars.name: All matching, not just this page
Pick up and gather
vars.def: The set is built by holding one item and tapping others to add them to the stack travelling with the finger or pointer; the selection exists only for the duration of the drag

vars.name: Drag across
vars.def: Dragging a finger continuously across several items toggles each one it passes over, without an explicit checkbox tap per item, e.g. Apple Photos multi-select on mobile

vars.name: Pick up and tap to add
vars.def: Grab one item, then tap additional items while still holding to add them to a stack under your finger, e.g. iOS Home Screen app stacking

dims.name: Action surface
dims.q: Where do bulk actions appear?

vars.name: Wizard
vars.def: A separate multistep flow (choose items, choose operation, confirm) launched from a menu command

vars.name: Side panel
vars.def: Bulk actions listed in a panel beside the collection while items are selected

vars.name: Wizard page
vars.def: The bulk operation leaves the collection for a dedicated multi-step page that chooses the items, the operation and its details before committing

vars.name: Keyboard shortcut
vars.def: No action surface appears at all — a key applies the action to everything selected, the norm in professional media tools where speed beats discoverability

vars.name: Command palette
vars.def: The action is typed into a searchable command surface (Cmd+K) that applies to the current selection, instead of appearing as a toolbar or a menu at the pointer

vars.name: Keyboard only
vars.def: Actions apply to the current selection via keyboard shortcuts directly, with no toolbar, menu or floating bar shown at all, e.g. Lightroom Classic flagging/rating shortcuts

dims.name: Consequence
dims.q: How is the consequence shown and reversed?

vars.name: Toast only
vars.def: A transient toast confirms the action; no count beforehand and no undo

dims.name: Execution
dims.q: When does it run?

entries.name: Card
entries.def: A bounded container that summarizes one item; the most common item view inside overviews.

dims.name: Card content
dims.q: What goes on the card?

dims.name: Form
dims.q: What shape and weight does the card take?

vars.name: Borderless
vars.def: No container at all: no fill, no border and no shadow — the media and text sit directly on the page background and the card is defined only by its grouping and spacing. The default for most modern consumer overviews, and not expressible with Material's three container styles

dims.name: Target
dims.q: Which part of the card opens the item?

vars.name: Separate targets per attribute
vars.def: Thumbnail opens a gallery, title opens the page

entries.name: Carousel
entries.def: A horizontally scrolling strip that shows a subset of items at once and hides the rest off-screen.

dims.name: Visible items
dims.q: How many items are visible, and how?

vars.name: Peek next
vars.def: The next item shows at the edge

dims.name: Advancing
dims.q: How does it move?

dims.name: Timing
dims.q: Does it move on its own?

dims.name: Position
dims.q: Does it say where you are?

entries.name: Drag to reorder
entries.def: Changing an item’s position, container or nesting by dragging it.

dims.name: Grab
dims.q: How is an item picked up?

vars.name: Drag anywhere
vars.def: Any point on the item is a grab point: a plain pointer press-and-drag with no handle and no hold delay

dims.name: Drop feedback
dims.q: How does the destination show itself?

dims.name: Destinations
dims.q: Where can it go?

dims.name: Long journeys
dims.q: What happens when the destination is off-screen?

entries.name: Filter controls
entries.def: Controls that narrow a collection to items whose attributes match chosen values.

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where do filters live?

vars.name: Toolbar popover
vars.def: Filter conditions live in a popover opened from a toolbar button, with no chips, sidebar, sheet or header controls

dims.name: Filter types
dims.q: What kinds of filter are offered?

vars.name: Map area
vars.def: Filter to what is in view

dims.name: Result preview
dims.q: Does a person see the effect before committing?

dims.name: Filter origin
dims.q: Who decides what can be filtered?

dims.name: Combination
dims.q: How do filters combine and persist?

entries.name: Property inspector
entries.def: A panel of key–value properties for the current selection, editable in place.

dims.name: Property set
dims.q: Which properties appear?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where does the inspector sit?

vars.name: Left sidebar
vars.def: The inspector panel opens on the left of the canvas

dims.name: Multi-selection
dims.q: What happens with several objects selected?

dims.name: Grouping
dims.q: How are properties organized?

dims.name: Applying changes
dims.q: When do edits take effect?

vars.name: Scrub to preview
vars.def: Drag a label to change a number

entries.name: Sort control
entries.def: A control that reorders a collection by one or more keys.

dims.name: Sort keys
dims.q: What can the collection be sorted by?

dims.name: Control form
dims.q: What does the control look like?

dims.name: Default order
dims.q: Who decides the default?

vars.name: Alphabetical
vars.def: Sorted by name A–Z by default

dims.name: Indicator
dims.q: How is the current order shown?

entries.name: Split pane
entries.def: Two or more resizable panes sharing one window, each holding its own view.

dims.name: Arrangement
dims.q: How are panes arranged and sized?

vars.name: Keyboard resize
vars.def: Panes are resized via keyboard shortcuts rather than dragging a divider with the pointer, e.g. tmux's prefix+arrow-key resize

dims.name: Pane relationship
dims.q: How do the panes relate?

vars.name: Linked selection
vars.def: Selecting in one drives the other

dims.name: Creating splits
dims.q: How is a split made?

vars.name: Drag a tab to an edge

dims.name: Persistence
dims.q: Does the layout survive?

vars.name: App-wide
vars.def: One layout remembered for the whole app or account and restored on every launch, not per session, per workspace, or as named layouts

vars.name: Remembered as a preference
vars.def: The layout is simply remembered for the application across restarts — no session boundary, no named layout to choose and no project to scope it to. The commonest case in shipping apps, and the codebook's three variations all imply an explicit container for the layout

entries.name: View switcher
entries.def: A control that changes how the same collection is represented.

dims.name: Views offered
dims.q: Which representations are available?

vars.name: Gallery
vars.def: Cards with a cover image per item

vars.name: Columns
vars.def: Miller columns, one per level of the hierarchy

dims.name: Control form
dims.q: How is a view picked?

dims.name: Persistence
dims.q: What remembers the choice?

vars.name: Named views shared with a team

dims.name: View independence
dims.q: Do views share filters and sorts?

entries.name: Collaborate
entries.def: Work on shared artifacts with others, at the same time or over time: see who is present, what changed, and what each person may do.

dims.name: Presence and authorship
dims.q: How are other people and their contributions made visible?

dims.name: Time mode
dims.q: Do people act together now, or across time?

dims.name: Access control
dims.q: What may each person see and change?

vars.name: Open to anyone with the link
Inherited from a container's membership
vars.def: Access is granted automatically to everyone already in a parent context (a chat channel, a shared folder) rather than assigned per-person, per-role, per-section, or by branch.

dims.name: Conflict handling
dims.q: How are concurrent or conflicting edits surfaced?

vars.name: Duplicate on conflict
vars.def: Both versions are kept as separate files rather than merged or overwritten (Dropbox conflicted copy, iCloud Drive)

vars.name: Conflicted copy kept alongside
vars.def: Neither edit is merged or discarded — the system keeps both as separate artifacts (a conflicted copy) and leaves the reconciliation to the people

entries.name: Annotation
entries.def: Attaching discussion or marks to a region of a shared artifact so feedback stays anchored to what it is about.

dims.name: Anchor form
dims.q: What is an annotation attached to?

vars.name: Block
vars.def: Attached to a whole block or paragraph rather than a text range or cell (Notion block comments)

vars.name: Content block
vars.def: Anchored to one whole structural block of a document (a paragraph, heading, or image), not a free text range, a canvas point, a timeline range, a spreadsheet cell/row, a code line, or the whole page.

dims.name: Marker presentation
dims.q: What does the annotation show in situ?

vars.name: Timeline marker
vars.def: A tick or dot on a media timeline at the annotated time (Frame.io, Loom, Vimeo review)

vars.name: Drawn mark
vars.def: A freehand shape drawn over the frame or page as the visible mark of the annotation, rather than a highlight, pin or glyph

dims.name: Thread layout
dims.q: Where does the conversation appear?

dims.name: Creating an annotation
dims.q: How is a new annotation started?

vars.name: Comment at the playhead
vars.def: The annotation takes the player's current position as its anchor with no selection or pin act at all — typing into the comment box is the whole gesture

dims.name: Thread lifecycle
dims.q: How do threads open, escalate and close?

dims.name: Annotation feedback
dims.q: How do people know annotations need attention?

entries.name: Co-editing presence
entries.def: Showing who else is in a shared artifact right now, where they are looking or editing, and how to follow or avoid colliding with them.

dims.name: Presence cues
dims.q: What awareness information is shown for each person?

vars.name: Ephemeral reactions or cursor chat
vars.def: Momentary expressive cues anchored at a person's cursor — a typed chat bubble, an emoji stamp, a high-five — beyond a static avatar, a named cursor, a selection highlight, a tool indicator, or an idle state.

dims.name: Where presence sits
dims.q: Where are presence cues placed?

dims.name: Awareness invocation
dims.q: How does a person engage another’s presence?

dims.name: Presence scope
dims.q: Whose activity is shown, and over what?

dims.name: Presence lifecycle
dims.q: When do presence cues appear and fade?

dims.name: Density adaptation
dims.q: How does presence behave when many people join?

entries.name: Sharing and permissions
entries.def: Granting, reviewing and revoking who can view, comment on or edit a shared artifact, and how they receive access.

dims.name: Permission model
dims.q: What rights can be granted?

dims.name: Share invocation
dims.q: How is sharing started?

dims.name: Permission scope
dims.q: What does a grant apply to?

dims.name: Sharing feedback
dims.q: How does the person know who has access and what changed?

dims.name: Grant lifecycle
dims.q: How do grants start, change and end?

dims.name: Policy initiative
dims.q: Who decides the default sharing posture?

entries.name: Version history
entries.def: A browsable record of past states of an artifact, with authorship, so a person can compare, restore or branch from an earlier version.

dims.name: What a version captures
dims.q: What is stored and shown for each version?

vars.name: Field change log
vars.def: Each version is one field's old and new value rather than a document state (Airtable record revisions)

vars.name: Field-level change log
vars.def: A record of individual field-by-field changes (old value to new value, who and when), rather than a snapshot of the whole document, a named checkpoint, a commit, an autosave generation, or a branch tip.

dims.name: History layout
dims.q: How is the history presented?

vars.name: Receding stack in 3D space
vars.def: Past states are shown as a stack of documents/windows receding visually into the distance, navigated by a timeline, rather than a flat chronological list, a calendar grouping, a filmstrip of thumbnails, a commit graph, or a diff view.

dims.name: Comparing versions
dims.q: How do versions relate when inspected?

dims.name: Restore flow
dims.q: How does a person return to or reuse a past state?

dims.name: Opening history
dims.q: How is history entered and left?

dims.name: History feedback
dims.q: How does the person know what will happen on restore?

entries.name: Communicate
entries.def: Exchange messages with people over time, from a live call to an email answered next week.

dims.name: Conversation structure
dims.q: How are exchanges divided?

vars.name: Proximity
vars.def: Exchanges are divided by location in a shared space: you talk to whoever is near your avatar, plus room-wide and everyone channels

vars.name: Proximity-based rooms
vars.def: Exchanges are not persistent named streams but form dynamically among people whose avatars are spatially near each other on a shared map

dims.name: Tempo
dims.q: How synchronous is it, and does it last?

dims.name: Arrangement
dims.q: How are conversations and messages arranged?

vars.name: Beside content
vars.def: A single conversation runs in a column alongside the primary content (a live video), with no list of other conversations

vars.name: Chat beside content
vars.def: A single persistent chat column runs beside a media stage (a live stream, a visit) rather than beside a navigable list of separate conversations

dims.name: Assistance
dims.q: What does the system write or summarize?

dims.name: Audience
dims.q: How many people is it for?

dims.name: Signals
dims.q: What does the system say about delivery and presence?

entries.name: Chat thread
entries.def: A chronological sequence of messages between participants, with a composer at the edge.

dims.name: Message layout
dims.q: How are messages drawn?

dims.name: Reply structure
dims.q: How do replies relate to messages?

dims.name: Message content
dims.q: What can a message carry, and what metadata shows?

dims.name: Message lifetime
dims.q: What happens to a message over time?

dims.name: Composer actions
dims.q: What can be done from the composer?

dims.name: Unread position
dims.q: Where does a returning reader land?

entries.name: Comment thread
entries.def: Discussion attached to an artifact or post, where replies nest and threads resolve.

dims.name: Nesting
dims.q: How do replies nest, and what are threads attached to?

vars.name: Anchored threads
vars.def: One thread per location in an artifact

dims.name: Ordering
dims.q: Who decides which comments come first?

vars.name: Anchor order
vars.def: Threads are listed in the order of their anchors in the artifact (page position, timecode), not by time or votes

vars.name: By anchor position
vars.def: Threads are ordered by where their anchors fall in the artifact — down the document, along the timeline, through the pages — not by time or votes

dims.name: Resolution
dims.q: Does a thread end?

vars.name: Marked status
vars.def: A thread can be marked completed/accepted/rejected but stays in view rather than being hidden

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where do threads appear?

vars.name: Inline at the anchor
vars.def: The thread is spliced into the artifact itself, pushing it apart — a review thread expanding under the diff line it annotates — rather than sitting in a margin or panel

vars.name: Bottom sheet
vars.def: Comments slide up as a sheet over the lower part of the screen while the content stays playing or visible above

vars.name: Inline at anchor
vars.def: The thread renders directly in the content flow at its anchored location (e.g., under a diff line) rather than offset to a margin column, a side panel, or as a pin on a canvas

dims.name: Long threads
dims.q: How are long threads condensed?

dims.name: Moderation
dims.q: How is the discussion kept healthy?

entries.name: Inbox
entries.def: A list of messages or requests awaiting attention, each opened, acted on and cleared.

dims.name: Organization
dims.q: How are messages sorted into places, and grouped?

dims.name: Reading arrangement
dims.q: Where does a message open, and how dense is the list?

dims.name: Triage model
dims.q: What does clearing a message mean?

vars.name: Close or solve
vars.def: Clearing means setting the ticket's status to solved/closed; assignment is a step along the way, not the clearing act

vars.name: Reading is triage
vars.def: Nothing is archived or filed: an item leaves the attention list simply by being read (HEY's Previously seen, Slack Activity)

vars.name: Mark as read
vars.def: Clearing means marking read: there is no destination, no archive and no file — the item simply stops being unread

dims.name: Row attributes
dims.q: What does each row show?

vars.name: Assignee
vars.def: The row shows who owns the item — an avatar or name for the teammate it is assigned to — which only exists in shared inboxes

vars.name: Status
vars.def: The row shows a workflow state the item moves through (new, open, pending, solved) and often a priority field, distinct from a user-applied label

dims.name: Prioritization
dims.q: Who decides what matters first?

dims.name: Deferral
dims.q: How can a message come back later?

entries.name: Video call
entries.def: Real-time audio and video among several participants, with shared content and side channels.

dims.name: Participant layout
dims.q: How are people and shared content arranged?

vars.name: Spatial tiles
vars.def: Participant tiles float in the user's physical room and can be placed freely, rather than in a grid or speaker layout

vars.name: Tiles placed in the room
vars.def: Each participant is a separate window the wearer positions in their own physical space; there is no shared arrangement and no self view

dims.name: Sub-spaces
dims.q: Can the call split?

vars.name: Persistent named rooms
vars.def: A server holds several always-on voice rooms that people move between by name, with no map or proximity

dims.name: Tile information
dims.q: What does a tile say?

dims.name: Meeting assistance
dims.q: What does the system capture or do?

dims.name: Attention controls
dims.q: What can each person hide or pin for themselves?

dims.name: Constraints
dims.q: How does it adapt to bandwidth and device?

entries.name: Reactions
entries.def: Lightweight responses attached to content without composing a message.

dims.name: Vocabulary
dims.q: What reactions exist?

vars.name: Graded intensity
vars.def: One reaction type whose value accumulates with repeated presses, so the reaction carries strength as well as existence (Medium's 1–50 claps)

dims.name: Aggregate
dims.q: What is shown about reactions?

dims.name: Adding
dims.q: How is a reaction added?

vars.name: Single tap
vars.def: One tap or click on a dedicated always-visible reaction button, with no picker to open and no gesture to learn — the heart under a post, the vote arrow

vars.name: Click to open picker
vars.def: Clicking (not hovering) a button reveals a picker of reaction options to choose from

vars.name: Tap a dedicated button
vars.def: A single click or tap on a dedicated reaction icon/button applies the platform's one default reaction directly — no gesture on the content itself, no revealed picker, no typed shortcut

dims.name: Social meaning
dims.q: Who sees a reaction?

entries.name: Configure and personalize
entries.def: Change how a system or a product behaves or looks.

dims.name: What is configured
dims.q: What kind of thing do the options describe?

vars.name: A resource being provisioned
vars.def: A cloud or service resource composed and priced before it is created (an instance, a database), neither a bought product nor an existing workspace

dims.name: Organization of options
dims.q: How are options grouped and found?

dims.name: Preview and apply
dims.q: When does a change become real, and can it be seen first?

dims.name: Scope of effect
dims.q: Who and what does a change affect?

entries.name: Product configurator
entries.def: Choosing options that compose a specific product instance — often with live preview, constraints and price — before purchase or build.

dims.name: Option model
dims.q: What kinds of choices make up the product?

dims.name: Preview
dims.q: How is the configured instance shown?

dims.name: Constraints and guidance
dims.q: How are illegal or poor combinations handled?

dims.name: Decision order
dims.q: In what order are choices presented?

dims.name: Price and commit
dims.q: How do cost and purchase enter the flow?

dims.name: Collaboration on a build
dims.q: Can more than one person shape the configuration?

entries.name: Settings
entries.def: A durable catalog of options that change how an app, account or device behaves, usually revisited rarely and in parts.

dims.name: Information architecture
dims.q: How are settings grouped and nested?

dims.name: Control types
dims.q: What kinds of values can be set?

dims.name: Discovery
dims.q: How does a person find the right setting?

dims.name: Application timing
dims.q: When do changes take effect?

dims.name: Scope and sync
dims.q: Where does a setting apply?

vars.name: Paired device
vars.def: Settings are configured on one device (e.g. a phone) but take effect on a different, paired device (e.g. a watch), rather than on the configuring device, the account everywhere, or a workspace

dims.name: Safety and reversibility
dims.q: How are risky changes handled?

entries.name: Consume media
entries.def: Watch, listen or read with control over pace, position and what comes next.

dims.name: Media kind
dims.q: What form does the media take?

dims.name: Transport and pace
dims.q: How does a person move through the media?

dims.name: What comes next
dims.q: What happens when this item ends?

vars.name: Queue
vars.def: An ordered list of what follows

dims.name: Attention surface
dims.q: How much of the screen does consumption own?

entries.name: Media player
entries.def: A stage and transport for playing video or audio, with position, quality and optional overlays under the person’s control.

dims.name: Transport controls
dims.q: Which playback controls are available?

dims.name: Position and chapters
dims.q: How is position shown and segmented?

dims.name: Presentation mode
dims.q: How is the player framed on screen?

vars.name: Standalone window
vars.def: A desktop player in its own resizable window, neither embedded in a page nor fullscreen by default

dims.name: Adaptation
dims.q: How does playback adapt to device and network?

dims.name: Overlays and assistance
dims.q: What appears on top of the media?

vars.name: Scene metadata overlay
vars.def: Information about what is on screen at this moment — the actors in this scene, the song playing, the product shown — surfaced over or beside the video and updating as it plays

dims.name: Session continuity
dims.q: How does playback resume across sessions?

entries.name: Playlist and queue
entries.def: An ordered list of media items that defines what plays now and what comes after, editable during consumption.

dims.name: Queue structure
dims.q: How is the upcoming sequence structured?

vars.name: Manual queue over a context
vars.def: Queue sits on top of an album or playlist

vars.name: Rule-built playlist
vars.def: The list is generated and maintained by a saved rule — these podcasts, sorted this way, this many episodes — and refills itself as new items arrive; neither hand-ordered nor algorithmically seeded

dims.name: Editing the order
dims.q: How does a person change what comes next?

dims.name: Order policy
dims.q: Who decides the order when the person does not?

dims.name: Item representation
dims.q: What does each queued item show?

vars.name: Tempo and key
vars.def: DJ software shows BPM, musical key and beat-grid state per track, which decide what can be mixed next

dims.name: Queue surface
dims.q: Where is the queue shown?

dims.name: Persistence
dims.q: Does the queue survive across sessions and devices?

entries.name: Reader
entries.def: Reading long-form text with control over typography, position, annotations and how much of the work is present.

dims.name: Typography and theme
dims.q: How does the text look?

dims.name: Pagination model
dims.q: How is the text chunked on screen?

dims.name: Navigation in the work
dims.q: How does a person move through chapters and locations?

dims.name: Annotations
dims.q: What can be attached to passages?

vars.name: Inline reader comments
vars.def: Readers attach public comments to a specific paragraph inside the text, visible to everyone else reading it — a conversation in the margin rather than a private mark or an aggregate of many private marks

dims.name: Reading assistance
dims.q: What does the reader contribute beyond the text?

dims.name: Progress and goals
dims.q: How is progress through the work tracked?

vars.name: Pages left in chapter
vars.def: Progress is shown as a count of pages remaining in the current chapter rather than time or percent

entries.name: Stories
entries.def: Full-bleed, timed, ephemeral frames advanced by tap or wait, usually from people you follow and gone within a day.

dims.name: Frame content
dims.q: What can a frame hold?

dims.name: Advance and pace
dims.q: How do frames advance?

dims.name: Tray and order
dims.q: How are authors ordered in the tray?

dims.name: Ephemerality
dims.q: How long do frames last, and can they persist?

vars.name: No expiry
vars.def: Frames persist indefinitely at a stable URL or in a library, with no archive step needed

vars.name: 48-hour expiry
vars.def: A fixed expiry longer than a day

dims.name: Audience and privacy
dims.q: Who can see a frame?

vars.name: Just me
vars.def: The frames are personal and have no audience at all unless their owner explicitly shares one out — the story form used for a private artefact

dims.name: Presentation
dims.q: How is the story experienced on screen?

vars.name: On a profile
vars.def: Stories live on a profile page (highlight circles under the bio, a status behind the avatar) rather than in a tray, tab or column

entries.name: Create and compose
entries.def: Make an artifact by directly manipulating its parts: text, shapes, nodes, clips or code.

dims.name: Surface
dims.q: What kind of space holds the artifact?

vars.name: 3D scene
vars.def: A navigable three-dimensional space with a camera, where the artifact is objects in depth rather than marks on a plane — the surface of every 3D, CAD and XR authoring tool

dims.name: Object structure
dims.q: How are parts organized?

dims.name: Selection
dims.q: What can be acted on at once?

dims.name: Tool access
dims.q: How are tools reached?

vars.name: Command palette
vars.def: A searchable launcher for every command in the tool, opened by a shortcut and driven by typing the action's name; distinct from a toolbar, a contextual toolbar and from slash commands, which insert content into a document

dims.name: Generation
dims.q: How much does the tool make for you?

dims.name: Authorship
dims.q: How many people make it, and how?

entries.name: Canvas editor
entries.def: Arranging visual objects freely on a two-dimensional canvas, frames or artboards.

dims.name: Canvas model
dims.q: What kind of space is it?

dims.name: Object hierarchy
dims.q: How are objects nested and reused?

dims.name: Selection
dims.q: How are objects selected?

dims.name: Tools
dims.q: How are tools reached?

dims.name: Generation
dims.q: What does the tool make for you?

dims.name: Multiplayer
dims.q: How is working together shown?

dims.name: Responsiveness
dims.q: How do designs respond to size?

entries.name: Code editor
entries.def: Reading and writing source code with structure-aware tools around the text.

dims.name: Code representation
dims.q: What is shown alongside the text?

vars.name: Projections
vars.def: Alternative views that edit the same code

dims.name: Workspace layout
dims.q: How is the workspace arranged?

dims.name: Commands
dims.q: How are actions invoked?

dims.name: Assistance
dims.q: How much does the editor write?

dims.name: Change review
dims.q: How are changes reviewed?

dims.name: Collaboration
dims.q: How do people code together?

dims.name: Customization depth
dims.q: How far can the editor be changed?

entries.name: Document editor
entries.def: Composing a flowing, structured document of text and embedded media.

dims.name: Document model
dims.q: What is the document made of?

vars.name: Free-form containers
vars.def: The page is a plane and the document is independent containers — text boxes, ink, images — placed at arbitrary positions; nothing reflows, so the document has no single linear order (OneNote, and digital-paper note apps generally)

vars.name: Free-form canvas
vars.def: The document is a page onto which text and ink containers can be dropped and positioned freely, rather than flowing text, discrete blocks, markdown or structured source

dims.name: Formatting access
dims.q: How is formatting applied?

dims.name: Page and navigation
dims.q: How is the document laid out and navigated?

dims.name: Change tracking
dims.q: How are changes made visible?

dims.name: Writing assistance
dims.q: What does the editor contribute to the writing?

dims.name: Reading modes
dims.q: How does it adapt to focus and reading?

entries.name: Node editor
entries.def: Building logic or data flow by connecting nodes through typed ports.

dims.name: Graph semantics
dims.q: What does a connection mean, and how are graphs packaged?

dims.name: Node content
dims.q: What does a node show?

vars.name: Step summary
vars.def: The node is a titled card with an app icon and a one-line description of what it is configured to do, and has no visible ports — the shape of linear automation builders, where connections are implied by order and configuration lives in a side panel

dims.name: Arrangement
dims.q: How are nodes placed and edges drawn?

dims.name: Adding nodes
dims.q: How are nodes added?

dims.name: Execution feedback
dims.q: How does the graph report what it did?

entries.name: Timeline editor
entries.def: Composing time-based media by arranging clips on tracks against a time axis.

dims.name: Track model
dims.q: How is time laid out?

dims.name: Nesting
dims.q: How are clips combined?

dims.name: Clip representation
dims.q: How does a clip show its content?

vars.name: Keyframes on property rows
vars.def: The lane holds parameter values over time — keyframes, envelopes, automation curves — rather than a piece of media, which is how motion and audio tools spend most of their timeline rows

dims.name: Edit operations
dims.q: What edits are possible, and on what?

vars.name: Ripple
vars.def: Later clips move with the edit

vars.name: Delete words
vars.def: Edit video by deleting transcript text

dims.name: Navigation
dims.q: How does a person move through time?

dims.name: Automation
dims.q: What does the editor do for you?

vars.name: Auto-assemble
vars.def: The editor builds a first cut from chosen media on its own (iMovie Magic Movie, template auto-fill), which the person then trims

vars.name: Auto-assemble from media
vars.def: The tool builds a whole edit from a pile of clips — choosing, ordering, trimming and scoring it — and hands back a timeline to adjust (iMovie Magic Movie, highlight-reel generators)

entries.name: Delegate to AI
entries.def: Hand a model a goal, then steer, verify and accept its work—keeping intent, progress and provenance visible enough to trust or reject the result.

dims.name: Handoff form
dims.q: How is intent handed to the model?

dims.name: Initiative balance
dims.q: Who drives the next step?

dims.name: Verification
dims.q: How does the person know what the model did and whether to trust it?

dims.name: Acceptance scope
dims.q: What can be accepted, edited or undone?

entries.name: Agent run
entries.def: A goal-directed model session that plans and executes multiple steps with tools, while the person monitors, interrupts, approves and reviews the resulting changes.

dims.name: Goal briefing
dims.q: What specifies the agent’s job?

dims.name: Step composition
dims.q: How are steps, tools and artifacts structured?

dims.name: Run control
dims.q: How is a run started, steered and stopped?

dims.name: Autonomy lifecycle
dims.q: How long does the agent act without a person?

dims.name: Progress feedback
dims.q: How does the person see what the agent is doing?

vars.name: Live preview of the artifact
vars.def: The thing being built is rendered and running beside the trace — an app preview, a live document — so progress is judged from the artifact rather than from logs or diffs; the defining feedback of app-generation agents

vars.name: Cost and usage meter
vars.def: Tokens, dollars or context used shown as the run proceeds, so the person can judge whether to let it continue; standard in agents where the person pays per call

dims.name: Approval initiative
dims.q: When must a person act during the run?

vars.name: Approve at milestones
vars.def: The person approves a plan or a checkpoint (plan, milestone build, final handoff) rather than tool calls or the whole result at once

vars.name: Approve the plan
vars.def: The person acts once, before any tool runs, by reading and editing the proposed plan; after that the run is autonomous — neither a per-tool gate nor a final diff review

entries.name: AI chat
entries.def: A turn-taking conversation with a model where prompts and replies accumulate, and the person steers by following up, editing context or starting anew.

dims.name: Turn content
dims.q: What can a turn contain?

vars.name: Spoken reply
vars.def: The turn is synthesised speech, with no text rendered on the surface where it happens (a transcript may appear later or in a companion app); the only turn content a screenless assistant has

dims.name: Thread composition
dims.q: How do turns and side contexts relate?

dims.name: Composer invocation
dims.q: How is the next message started?

dims.name: Conversation flow
dims.q: How does the dialogue progress and recover?

vars.name: Hand off to an agent run
Barge-in
vars.def: Speaking over the model stops its reply and takes the turn, without a stop button or regenerate

vars.name: Barge-in duplex
vars.def: Either party may speak over the other: the person interrupts a reply mid-sentence and the model yields and re-plans, so turns overlap instead of alternating

vars.name: Hand off to a person
vars.def: The conversation is escalated out of the model to a human who continues in the same thread — the central recovery path in support chat, and the mirror image of handing off to an agent run

dims.name: Reply feedback
dims.q: How is generation and quality communicated?

dims.name: Context scope
dims.q: What does the model condition on?

entries.name: Generative variations
entries.def: A model produces multiple candidate outputs for one brief so a person can compare, pick, remix or regenerate along chosen dimensions.

dims.name: Candidate representation
dims.q: What does each variation show?

dims.name: Set composition
dims.q: How do candidates relate to the brief and each other?

dims.name: Comparison layout
dims.q: How are variations arranged for choice?

dims.name: Generation controls
dims.q: How does the person request or steer the set?

dims.name: Selection flow
dims.q: How does choosing proceed after candidates appear?

dims.name: Provenance feedback
dims.q: How are origin and parameters shown on candidates?

entries.name: Inline suggestion
entries.def: Model-proposed continuation or edit shown inside the artifact at the caret or selection, accepted, cycled or dismissed without leaving the editor.

dims.name: Suggestion content
dims.q: What form does the proposal take?

dims.name: Where it appears
dims.q: How is the suggestion placed relative to the artifact?

dims.name: Triggering
dims.q: What brings a suggestion up?

dims.name: Acceptance flow
dims.q: How are proposals taken, varied or refused?

vars.name: Apply then revert
vars.def: The proposal is written into the artifact immediately with no accept gate; refusing it means undoing — the acceptance model of rewrite commands in design and OS-level writing tools

dims.name: Suggestion initiative
dims.q: How assertive is the model?

dims.name: Confidence feedback
dims.q: How is suggestion quality or origin shown?

entries.name: AI provenance
entries.def: Visible markers of what a model produced, from which sources or tools, so a person can judge trust, reuse and responsibility.

dims.name: What is disclosed
dims.q: What provenance facts are shown?

vars.name: Verification highlighting
vars.def: Sentence-level colour highlighting showing whether a live search corroborates or contradicts the claim, rather than a citation list or a static badge

dims.name: Provenance placement
dims.q: Where do disclosure cues sit?

dims.name: Inspecting provenance
dims.q: How does a person open the full trail?

dims.name: Trust feedback
dims.q: How is uncertainty or risk communicated?

vars.name: Blanket disclaimer
vars.def: A standing warning attached to every output regardless of content — ChatGPT can make mistakes, AI responses may include mistakes, AI-generated content may be incorrect — rather than a cue about this claim, these sources or this retrieval

entries.name: Prompt input
entries.def: The control where a person enters or edits the instruction, context and attachments sent to a model.

dims.name: Input content
dims.q: What can the composer hold?

dims.name: Composer layout
dims.q: Where does the prompt UI sit?

vars.name: Centred hero box
vars.def: A large prompt box in the middle of an empty page that becomes the bottom composer once a thread starts

vars.name: Terminal prompt line
vars.def: A readline-style input at the bottom of a terminal transcript, with slash commands and mentions typed in place

dims.name: Submitting
dims.q: How is the prompt sent?

vars.name: Open mic
vars.def: Nothing is pressed or held to send — the microphone stays open and voice activity detection ends the turn, which is what separates modern voice modes from push-to-talk

dims.name: Composer assistance
dims.q: What help shapes the prompt before send?

entries.name: Suggestion chips
entries.def: Compact, tappable proposed prompts or next actions that fill or refine the composer when selected.

dims.name: Chip content
dims.q: What does a chip propose?

dims.name: Chip placement
dims.q: Where do chips appear?

dims.name: Chip selection
dims.q: What happens when a chip is chosen?

dims.name: Chip lifecycle
dims.q: When do chips refresh or disappear?

entries.name: Enter and edit data
entries.def: Give a system structured information, have it checked, and correct it — from a single field to a multi-page application.

dims.name: Field organization
dims.q: How are fields grouped and paced?

dims.name: Input modality
dims.q: How does information get in?

dims.name: Prefill
dims.q: How much does the system fill in?

dims.name: Validation timing
dims.q: When is input checked?

vars.name: None
vars.def: Input is never checked; whatever is typed or picked is accepted as-is (Notion properties, plain note fields)

dims.name: Commit model
dims.q: When is input saved?

entries.name: Form
entries.def: A set of labelled fields that collects structured data and submits it together.

dims.name: Field layout
dims.q: How are labels and fields arranged?

vars.name: Conversational prompt
vars.def: The question is asked as a chat message; there is no persistent field label, only a bare input for the reply.

vars.name: Prompt bubble
vars.def: The question is a chat message in the conversation above a shared composer; no label is attached to the control itself

dims.name: Grouping
dims.q: How are fields grouped?

dims.name: Validation
dims.q: When and how are problems shown?

vars.name: None
vars.def: Input is never checked; the form accepts whatever is entered (fillable PDFs, contact cards, password-manager items)

dims.name: Prefill
dims.q: What arrives already filled?

vars.name: From account profile
vars.def: Fields arrive filled from the product's own stored profile or record (LinkedIn Easy Apply contact info, MyChart chart data, Zocdoc patient details) — neither the browser nor a document

vars.name: Autofill from a profile
vars.def: Fields arrive filled from the person's own stored account profile or record in this product, not from the browser — the archetype entry already has this variation and the form entry lacks it

vars.name: Looked up from records
vars.def: Fields arrive filled from a third-party or public-records lookup keyed on what the person has already given (insurance quotes filling in your vehicles and household drivers)

dims.name: Help
dims.q: What helps a person answer?

dims.name: Commit
dims.q: How is the form saved?

vars.name: Save the file
vars.def: The filled form is a document the person saves or sends themselves; there is no submit to a system at all

entries.name: Spreadsheet
entries.def: A grid of cells holding values and formulas, where the person defines both the structure and the computation.

dims.name: Cell content
dims.q: What can a cell hold?

vars.name: Action buttons
vars.def: A cell holds a button that runs an action (add a row, call an automation) rather than a value

dims.name: Structure
dims.q: How much structure is imposed on the grid?

vars.name: Tables on a canvas
vars.def: There is no underlying grid at all: each table is a separate object placed on a free canvas beside charts and text (Apple Numbers)

vars.name: Tables in a canvas or document
vars.def: There is no endless grid: tables are objects placed on a page, canvas or inside prose, and the document rather than the sheet is the container

dims.name: Visual encoding
dims.q: How are values made visible?

dims.name: Views
dims.q: How can the same grid be looked at?

vars.name: Non-grid views
vars.def: The same rows can be looked at as a board, calendar, timeline or gallery — every variation of views as written assumes the grid stays a grid

dims.name: Concurrency
dims.q: How do several people work on it?

dims.name: Assistance
dims.q: What does the software fill in for you?

vars.name: Cleanup suggestions
vars.def: The software proposes corrections to values already entered — inconsistent spellings, bad types — instead of filling new ones in

entries.name: Wizard
entries.def: A multi-step flow that breaks a complex task into ordered screens, often branching on earlier answers.

dims.name: Sequence
dims.q: How do steps connect, and can the task be resumed?

dims.name: Progress
dims.q: How is progress shown?

vars.name: Step counter
vars.def: Step n of m as a bare count, with no step titles (Slack workspace creation)

dims.name: Step density
dims.q: How much is asked per step?

dims.name: Presentation
dims.q: Where does the wizard live?

dims.name: Review
dims.q: Can everything be reviewed before committing?

dims.name: Assistance
dims.q: Does the system help answer?

entries.name: Autocomplete
entries.def: Suggestions that appear as a person types, completing or replacing the input.

dims.name: Suggestion types
dims.q: What is suggested?

vars.name: Text continuation
vars.def: The suggestion continues the prose or code being written (next words, a sentence, a code block) rather than completing a query or naming an entity

vars.name: Places and addresses
vars.def: Street addresses, cities, regions or venues from a geocoder or place index — the codebook's own 'address' frame has no type for them

vars.name: Records or entities
vars.def: Objects from a known set — addresses, places, records — listed as plain rows with no artwork; the existing entity variation requires images

vars.name: Code symbols
vars.def: Identifiers, methods and keywords from the code's symbol table, each carrying a type icon and documentation.

vars.name: Symbols in scope
vars.def: Identifiers, methods and properties that are legal at the cursor, offered with their type and documentation

dims.name: Source
dims.q: Where do suggestions come from?

dims.name: Presentation
dims.q: How are suggestions shown?

vars.name: Suggestion bar
vars.def: A horizontal strip of a few candidates above a keyboard or input, not a list and not inline (iOS QuickType)

dims.name: Acceptance
dims.q: How is a suggestion taken?

dims.name: Freedom
dims.q: Must the value come from the suggestions?

entries.name: Choice control
entries.def: A control for picking one or several options from a known set.

dims.name: Cardinality
dims.q: How many can be chosen?

dims.name: Form
dims.q: What does the control look like?

dims.name: Option content
dims.q: What does an option say?

dims.name: Effect timing
dims.q: When does a choice take effect?

dims.name: Many options
dims.q: What happens when the set is large?

entries.name: Colour picker
entries.def: A control for choosing a colour, by sight, by value or by name.

dims.name: Form
dims.q: How is colour space presented?

vars.name: Palette bars with regenerate
vars.def: Several colours (a whole palette) are randomized together by a single action, rather than one colour picked at a time via a field, wheel, sliders or swatches.

dims.name: Colour model
dims.q: In what model is colour expressed?

vars.name: CMYK
vars.def: Colour expressed as cyan, magenta, yellow, black for print (Illustrator Color panel in a print document, GIMP and macOS Colors CMYK tabs)

dims.name: Helpers
dims.q: What helps a person choose?

dims.name: Target
dims.q: What does the colour apply to?

vars.name: The active tool or brush
vars.def: The colour is loaded into the tool and applies to whatever is painted next, rather than to an object that already exists or to a token

entries.name: Date picker
entries.def: A control for choosing a date, a time or a range of dates.

dims.name: Presentation
dims.q: How is time presented for choosing?

vars.name: Dropdowns per part
vars.def: Each part of the date and time is its own select (month, day, year, hour, minute) — no calendar, no free typing (Windows Set the date and time)

vars.name: Week strip with paging
vars.def: A row of individual days, often with time slots shown beneath each, that pages forward or back by arrows — distinct from a month-grid popover, an always-visible inline calendar, scroll wheels, a formatted text field or natural language.

dims.name: Selection
dims.q: What is being chosen?

vars.name: Recurring rule
vars.def: What is chosen is a repetition — every Friday, the first of each month — rather than a date, a range or a set of dates

dims.name: Day annotations
dims.q: What does each day say?

dims.name: Opening
dims.q: What opens it?

dims.name: Locale
dims.q: How does it adapt to the person’s conventions?

entries.name: File upload
entries.def: Handing files to a system: choosing them, sending them and seeing that they arrived.

dims.name: Entry
dims.q: How do files get in?

vars.name: Automatic sync
vars.def: Files enter with no per-file action: a folder or camera roll is watched and uploaded on its own (Google Photos backup, Dropbox desktop folder)

vars.name: Automatic from the device
vars.def: Files are handed over with no act of choosing at all — a background service uploads what the device produces once it is switched on

dims.name: Progress
dims.q: How is the upload shown?

vars.name: Overall progress
vars.def: One indicator for the whole batch or send rather than one per file (WeTransfer's ring, iMessage's send bar)

dims.name: Multiplicity
dims.q: How many files at once?

dims.name: Preview
dims.q: What is shown about each file?

dims.name: Checks
dims.q: When are files checked?

entries.name: Inline edit
entries.def: Editing a value where it is displayed, without a separate form.

dims.name: Entering edit mode
dims.q: How does a displayed value become editable?

dims.name: Commit
dims.q: When does the edit save?

dims.name: Saved state
dims.q: How does a person know it saved?

dims.name: Unit
dims.q: What is edited at once?

entries.name: Rating
entries.def: An input for expressing quality or preference on a scale.

dims.name: Scale
dims.q: What scale is used?

dims.name: Context
dims.q: What accompanies the rating?

vars.name: Quick tags
vars.def: Predefined chips or checkboxes accompany the score — compliment badges, feedback tags, what-went-wrong lists (Uber, Lyft, ChatGPT, Teams, Zoom)

vars.name: Reason or compliment tags
vars.def: A fixed vocabulary of reasons or compliments offered after the score — usually revealed by a low or high rating — which is neither free prose nor a per-aspect scale

dims.name: Moment
dims.q: When is a rating asked for?

dims.name: Visibility
dims.q: Who sees it?

entries.name: Slider
entries.def: A control for choosing a value or range by dragging along a track.

dims.name: Values
dims.q: What is chosen?

dims.name: Labels
dims.q: What does the track tell you?

dims.name: Scale
dims.q: How are values spread along the track?

dims.name: Precision
dims.q: How can a precise value be reached?

vars.name: Slow scrubbing
vars.def: Move the finger away to slow down

vars.name: Scrub the label
vars.def: Dragging directly on the numeric value's own label changes it, without needing to open or grab a visible track.

entries.name: Tag input
entries.def: An input that turns typed or chosen values into removable tokens.

dims.name: Token content
dims.q: What does a token show?

dims.name: Vocabulary
dims.q: Can new values be created?

dims.name: Creating tokens
dims.q: What turns text into a token?

vars.name: Space
vars.def: Pressing the space bar also turns the typed text into a token, alongside or instead of Enter/comma.

dims.name: Overflow
dims.q: What happens with many tokens?

vars.name: Stacked list
vars.def: Tokens leave the input and become a vertical list of rows beneath it, one per value, each with its own remove control

vars.name: Stacked list of rows
vars.def: Each added value becomes its own full-width row in a vertical list, rather than an inline chip that wraps, scrolls on one line, or collapses into a count.

entries.name: Text field
entries.def: A single- or multi-line input for typed text, together with its label, help and validation.

dims.name: Supporting content
dims.q: What surrounds the input?

vars.name: Format examples
vars.def: A worked example of the expected format (e.g. QQ 12 34 56 C) shown alongside the field — the 'form' entry's Help dimension has this exact variation, but this entry's Supporting-content options don't.

vars.name: Reveal toggle
vars.def: An eye/show icon toggles a sensitive value between masked dots and its plain text, distinct from a label, placeholder, hint, counter, prefix/suffix or clear button.

dims.name: Validation
dims.q: How is input checked?

vars.name: On submit
vars.def: The field is checked only when the form or step is submitted (GOV.UK, Google sign-in Next, Amazon Apply)

dims.name: Style
dims.q: How is the field drawn?

dims.name: Assistance
dims.q: What does the system add while typing?

dims.name: Input type
dims.q: How does the field adapt to what is typed?

vars.name: Obscured entry
vars.def: The characters are hidden as they are typed, usually with a reveal toggle — a password or secret field

entries.name: Explore space
entries.def: Understand, navigate and select within a spatial world — geographic, diagrammatic, seating or three-dimensional — where position itself carries meaning.

dims.name: Projection and scale
dims.q: How is the spatial world projected, and at what scale?

dims.name: Navigation of the viewport
dims.q: How does a person move through space?

vars.name: Locomotion
vars.def: Continuous first-person movement by joystick or keys through a 3D world, distinct from teleporting

vars.name: Move your body
vars.def: The viewport moves because the person moves: in AR and room-scale XR the camera is the device, so walking, leaning and turning are the navigation

dims.name: Located content
dims.q: What kinds of things appear in space, and how abstracted are they?

vars.name: Authored objects
vars.def: Shapes, frames, drawings and content people create as the substance of the space itself, as opposed to annotations laid over something else

vars.name: Placed models
vars.def: Virtual objects anchored into the real room at true scale

vars.name: Continuous field
vars.def: A scalar or vector field rendered across the whole world — wind particles, temperature shading, rainfall — rather than discrete located things

dims.name: Selection and detail
dims.q: How does selecting in space open further information?

entries.name: Map explorer
entries.def: A pannable, zoomable geographic map with layers of places, routes or data, used to find, compare and open things in the world.

dims.name: Base and overlays
dims.q: What is drawn on the map, and how are overlays chosen?

dims.name: Viewport controls
dims.q: How does the person change what region is shown?

vars.name: Bounds fit to results
vars.def: Zoom to fit a result set

dims.name: Map and list coupling
dims.q: How do the map and any list or detail of the same items relate?

dims.name: Mark encoding
dims.q: How do attributes become visual marks?

dims.name: Filtering the world
dims.q: How is the set of visible places narrowed?

dims.name: Context and device
dims.q: How does the map change with mobility, offline and screen size?

entries.name: 3D object viewer
entries.def: A three-dimensional model presented for inspection — orbit, pan, zoom and sometimes explode or cross-section — to understand form, fit or configuration.

dims.name: What the model shows
dims.q: How much of the object’s structure and metadata is exposed?

vars.name: Abstract representation
vars.def: Domain-specific renderings that are neither photoreal nor wireframe — molecular ribbons, sticks and surfaces, schematic shading — where the representation is a scientific convention rather than a material

dims.name: Camera control
dims.q: How does the person change viewpoint?

vars.name: Move the device
vars.def: In phone AR the viewpoint is the device camera; the person changes view by moving the phone, while gestures move the object

dims.name: Part selection and detail
dims.q: How does selecting geometry open information?

dims.name: Viewer chrome
dims.q: How is the 3D view arranged with controls and metadata?

dims.name: Loading and fidelity
dims.q: How does the model arrive and refine?

dims.name: Guidance
dims.q: Who directs attention in the scene?

entries.name: Seat map
entries.def: A diagram of a venue’s seats or sections where people browse availability and price, then select one or more seats to book.

dims.name: Seat content
dims.q: What does each seat or section reveal before selection?

vars.name: Value score per section
vars.def: The section is summarised by a computed quality or value rating (SeatGeek's Deal Score) rather than by its lowest price, its remaining count or whether it is sold out

dims.name: Diagram structure
dims.q: How is the venue decomposed, and how does selection nest?

dims.name: Map interaction
dims.q: How do people navigate the diagram and pick seats?

dims.name: Availability encoding
dims.q: How are price and status shown visually?

dims.name: Selection rules
dims.q: What constraints apply to the set of chosen seats?

dims.name: Hold and purchase timing
dims.q: How long are seats kept while the person decides?

entries.name: Zoomable canvas
entries.def: An unbounded 2D plane of free-placed objects that is navigated by pan and zoom, used to organize, present or explore spatial arrangements of content.

dims.name: Object content
dims.q: What lives on the canvas, and how much detail shows at a glance?

vars.name: Frame as portal
vars.def: Enter a frame for denser content

dims.name: Spatial structure
dims.q: How are objects related in space?

vars.name: Graph with edges
vars.def: Nodes and links on a plane

dims.name: Viewport navigation
dims.q: How does the person move and orient?

dims.name: Canvas chrome
dims.q: What UI surrounds the plane?

dims.name: Collaboration on the plane
dims.q: How are other people and their changes shown?

dims.name: Purpose of the canvas
dims.q: Is the canvas primarily for making, facilitating or consuming?

vars.name: Guided path
vars.def: The canvas is consumed along an authored camera path — the author lays topics out in space and presenting flies between them in a set order — which is neither free read-only exploration nor live facilitation

entries.name: Guide and onboard
entries.def: Learn a system while using it: first-run introductions, help at the moment of a question, and support when stuck.

dims.name: Trigger
dims.q: What brings help up?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where does help appear?

vars.name: Live session
vars.def: The guidance is delivered by a person in a scheduled call or screen share rather than placed anywhere in the interface — onboarding as a service, common in high-touch and enterprise products

dims.name: Progression
dims.q: How does learning advance?

dims.name: Guide
dims.q: Who or what guides?

dims.name: Experience level
dims.q: Does guidance change with expertise?

entries.name: Contextual help
entries.def: Explanations available where a question arises, without leaving the task.

dims.name: Access
dims.q: How is help asked for?

vars.name: Hover
vars.def: Hover or a modifier-click on the item itself brings help, with no icon, link or menu

vars.name: The control itself
vars.def: Help is asked for by pointing at or modifier-clicking the object being explained — a rich tooltip on hover, an Option-click on a symbol — rather than by a separate help affordance placed next to it

dims.name: Content
dims.q: What kind of help is given?

vars.name: Shortcut reference
vars.def: A list of keyboard shortcuts and their actions

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where does help appear?

vars.name: Inline with the field
vars.def: The help is printed in the layout beside or beneath the control it explains, taking up space and needing no interaction — GOV.UK hint text, form helper text, empty-field descriptions

vars.name: Inline static text
vars.def: Help text sits permanently visible beside or under the field itself, needing no popover, panel or overlay to reveal it, e.g. GOV.UK hint text

dims.name: Proactivity
dims.q: Does help wait to be asked?

dims.name: Relevance
dims.q: How specific is it?

vars.name: Whole product
vars.def: Help searched or listed for the whole product, not tied to the current page or field

entries.name: Onboarding tour
entries.def: A sequence of screens or coach marks that introduces a product’s key features on first use.

dims.name: Form
dims.q: What does the tour look like?

vars.name: Sample content
vars.def: A pre-filled sample document, board or base whose own contents explain the product

vars.name: Live session
vars.def: A scheduled call with a person who walks through the product

dims.name: Progression
dims.q: How does a person move through it?

dims.name: Action required
dims.q: Does the person do or just read?

dims.name: Personalization
dims.q: Is the tour the same for everyone?

vars.name: Adapts to what was already done

dims.name: Re-access
dims.q: Can it be revisited?

entries.name: Empty state
entries.def: What a view shows when it has nothing in it yet, or when nothing matches.

dims.name: Cause and content
dims.q: Why is it empty, and what is shown?

dims.name: Starter content
dims.q: Does the system offer a head start?

vars.name: Recommendations
vars.def: System-picked items offered to add as a head start

vars.name: Suggested items
vars.def: The head start is a set of real items the system picks — songs for an empty playlist, nearby homes when nothing matched — rather than a template, sample data or something generated from a prompt

dims.name: Recovery
dims.q: What gets a person out of emptiness?

vars.name: Suggested searches
vars.def: Alternative queries or related items offered as the way out of no results

vars.name: Request access
vars.def: A button to ask the owner for permission

vars.name: Try another query
vars.def: The way out is changing the search itself — spelling advice, broader terms, suggested alternative queries — which is the commonest no-results recovery and is not the same as clearing filters

entries.name: Tooltip
entries.def: A short label or explanation that appears on hover or focus.

dims.name: Shown on
dims.q: What brings it up?

dims.name: Timing
dims.q: When does it appear and leave?

vars.name: Until dismissed
vars.def: Opened by a click and stays until closed or clicked away

dims.name: Content
dims.q: What does it say?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where does it sit?

vars.name: Below
vars.def: Fixed under the target, as for top toolbars

entries.name: Monitor and get notified
entries.def: Keep track of changing state, and be interrupted only when it matters.

dims.name: Signals
dims.q: What is being watched?

dims.name: Surfaces
dims.q: Where does change appear?

vars.name: On the object
vars.def: Change shows inside the watched object's own screen (an order page, a tracking view, the city's weather page) rather than on a separate monitoring surface

vars.name: In-app banner
vars.def: A persistent coloured strip inside the app's own view carrying the condition — not a list, a badge, an ambient chrome indicator or an interruption; the archetype has a banner component but Surfaces has no variation for it

dims.name: Delivery timing
dims.q: When does a change reach the person?

dims.name: What matters
dims.q: Who decides what is worth attention?

dims.name: Severity
dims.q: How is urgency expressed?

vars.name: Status colour with icon and label

dims.name: Granularity
dims.q: At what level is state reported?

entries.name: Activity log
entries.def: A time-ordered record of what happened to an object or account, and who did it.

dims.name: Event detail
dims.q: How much does each event say?

dims.name: Subject
dims.q: Whose activity is it?

dims.name: Aggregation
dims.q: Are events combined?

dims.name: Presentation
dims.q: How is the record drawn?

dims.name: Acting on history
dims.q: Can the past be restored from the log?

vars.name: Erase the record
vars.def: Entries can be deleted from the log — removing the record (and sometimes the content it refers to) rather than restoring, reverting or replaying anything; the characteristic action of personal-data activity logs

entries.name: Dashboard
entries.def: Several metrics and states on one view, arranged to be scanned at a glance and drilled into.

dims.name: Widgets and purpose
dims.q: What goes on the dashboard, and what is it for?

vars.name: Categorical charts
vars.def: Bar, column, pie or scatter comparing categories rather than time — the commonest BI widget after the KPI tile, and the list jumps from time-series straight to tables

vars.name: Control widgets
vars.def: Widgets that act on the thing being monitored — a switch, slider, scene button or camera with a talk control — rather than only reporting it; smart-home and admin dashboards are built from these

vars.name: Categorical chart
vars.def: A bar/column chart encoding a categorical dimension rather than a time series (e.g., sales by category, top pages) — the codebook's Time-series charts doesn't cover non-temporal charts

dims.name: Arrangement
