dims.q: How are widgets placed, and how many?

dims.name: Linking
dims.q: How do widgets affect each other?

vars.name: Cross-filtering
vars.def: Clicking a mark filters the rest

dims.name: Refresh
dims.q: How current is it?

vars.name: On visit
vars.def: Current data is fetched when the page is opened and then sits still until it is reloaded — neither a frozen exported snapshot nor an auto-refreshing or streaming view; the default for consumer and SaaS web dashboards

dims.name: Alerting
dims.q: How does it call attention to change?

dims.name: Ownership
dims.q: Whose dashboard is it?

entries.name: Notification center
entries.def: A collected list of notifications from many sources, reviewed and cleared after the fact.

dims.name: Grouping
dims.q: How are notifications bundled?

dims.name: What arrives
dims.q: What decides which notifications get through?

dims.name: Clearing
dims.q: How does a notification leave?

vars.name: Mark read
vars.def: The item never leaves: viewing it or an explicit Mark as read only clears its unread styling (social feeds, Slack Activity, Jira, Teams, Discord)

vars.name: Read on view
vars.def: The notification is never removed — opening the surface or the item only clears its unread state, and the entry stays in the list until it ages out; the default in social and activity feeds, and distinct from an explicit Dismiss or Done

dims.name: Item content
dims.q: What does a notification show?

dims.name: Surface
dims.q: Where does the list live?

dims.name: Bulk handling
dims.q: How are many handled at once?

entries.name: Status tracker
entries.def: Showing where a process, order or journey is in its sequence of stages, and what happens next.

dims.name: Stage model
dims.q: How is progress structured?

dims.name: Stage detail
dims.q: What does each stage tell you?

dims.name: Presentation
dims.q: Where and how is status shown?

vars.name: Status statement
vars.def: The current state is written out as a sentence or paragraph with no sequence drawn — no bar, timeline or map; the common government casework shape, where the wording carries everything

vars.name: Narrative status text
vars.def: The current stage is conveyed as a plain-language paragraph rather than a bar, timeline or map — typical of government casework portals

dims.name: Updates
dims.q: How does status reach the person?

dims.name: Exceptions
dims.q: What happens when progress stalls?

entries.name: Badge
entries.def: A small indicator on another element showing a count or a status.

dims.name: Meaning
dims.q: What does the badge say?

dims.name: Overflow
dims.q: How are large counts shown?

dims.name: What counts
dims.q: Who decides what increments it?

vars.name: Pending actions
vars.def: The badge counts work waiting for the person — updates to install, apps to update, tasks to finish — rather than anything read, unread or addressed to them; the counting rules as written assume a message inbox

dims.name: Aggregation
dims.q: Does it roll up?

vars.name: Device total
vars.def: One indicator for every unread notification on the device, on system chrome rather than on any app's icon or nav entry (watch faces, always-on displays)

entries.name: Banner
entries.def: A persistent message across a region or page about a condition that needs attention.

dims.name: Scope
dims.q: What does the condition apply to?

dims.name: Severity
dims.q: How serious is it?

dims.name: Dismissal
dims.q: Can it go away?

dims.name: Action
dims.q: Does it offer a way to fix things?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where does it sit?

entries.name: Progress indicator
entries.def: Showing that work is happening, and how far along it is.

dims.name: Determinacy
dims.q: How much does it say about remaining work?

dims.name: Form
dims.q: What does it look like?

vars.name: Text status
vars.def: A word or short phrase (Saving…, Posting…) with at most a small icon and no geometric progress indicator

dims.name: Delay handling
dims.q: When does it appear?

dims.name: Coverage
dims.q: What does it block?

dims.name: Control
dims.q: Can the work be stopped?

entries.name: Stat tile
entries.def: A compact tile showing one key number with its context: label, change and trend.

dims.name: Context
dims.q: What gives the number meaning?

dims.name: Change encoding
dims.q: How is change drawn?

dims.name: Time window
dims.q: Over what period?

dims.name: Drill-down
dims.q: What is behind the number?

entries.name: Toast
entries.def: A brief, non-blocking message about the outcome of an action that goes away on its own.

dims.name: Duration
dims.q: How long does it stay?

dims.name: Content
dims.q: What does it carry?

dims.name: Position
dims.q: Where does it appear?

vars.name: Bottom right stack
vars.def: Cards slide in and stack in the lower-right corner (VS Code notifications, sonner-style dashboards)

vars.name: Centre of screen
vars.def: A pill or HUD in the middle of the screen over the content, in the manner of Apple's Music/volume HUDs

vars.name: Centre overlay
vars.def: A pill or HUD floating at the centre of the screen over the content, the iOS system-confirmation shape; not anchored to an edge or to the control that caused it

dims.name: Severity
dims.q: What kind of outcome is it?

entries.name: Navigate and wayfind
entries.def: Know where you are, where you can go, and get there — the structure of places in a product and the means of moving between them.

dims.name: Structure
dims.q: How are places related to each other?

vars.name: Hub and spoke
vars.def: Return to a home between tasks

dims.name: Persistent navigation
dims.q: Where do the always-available routes live?

vars.name: Hardware-summoned overlay
vars.def: The persistent navigation surface has no fixed onscreen position at all; it's summoned from anywhere by a physical control (a crown, a controller button) and floats over whatever app is running.

dims.name: Wayfinding cues
dims.q: How does a person know where they are?

vars.name: Address
vars.def: A readable, editable URL or path

vars.name: Where it sits in the room
vars.def: In spatial computing the cue to where you are is the position and persistence of the window or panel in the physical space, not a label on a screen

dims.name: Routes
dims.q: How does a person move?

vars.name: Content links
vars.def: Moving by following a link inside the content itself — a word in a sentence, a related-article card — rather than through any navigation control; the primary route on the networked web and absent from the list

dims.name: Across devices
dims.q: How does navigation change with screen size?

vars.name: Split view becomes stack
vars.def: A sidebar-and-detail split on large screens collapses into a single column navigated by pushing and back, not a drawer or tabs (iOS Settings, Mail, Notes on iPhone)

vars.name: Split view collapses to a stack
vars.def: A sidebar-plus-detail layout on a large screen becomes a drill-down stack with a back button on a small one — the standard iPadOS/iOS behaviour, which is neither a drawer, bottom tabs nor a rail

vars.name: Top bar collapses to a menu button
vars.def: A persistent top navigation bar collapses into a hamburger/menu-button-revealed list as the screen narrows, rather than a sidebar transforming into tabs, a drawer, or a rail — the responsive dimension's four variations all assume a sidebar-based desktop layout to start from.

entries.name: App shell
entries.def: The persistent frame around an application’s content: global navigation, identity, search, and the region where content changes.

dims.name: Navigation placement
dims.q: Where are primary and secondary navigation?

vars.name: Tab bar that expands to sidebar

dims.name: Navigation items
dims.q: What does navigation contain, and how does it change?

dims.name: Show and hide
dims.q: Is the shell always there?

dims.name: Responsive shell
dims.q: What happens as the screen narrows?

dims.name: Workspace structure
dims.q: How many applications or workspaces does one shell hold?

entries.name: Command palette
entries.def: A keyboard-summoned search box that finds and runs commands, jumps to places and objects, and teaches shortcuts along the way.

dims.name: Results
dims.q: What can be found, and what does each result show?

vars.name: People
vars.def: Finding and jumping to a specific person, distinct from a command, a place, a file, a settings toggle, a system/web result, or an AI answer.

vars.name: Code symbols
vars.def: Classes, symbols and other code-structure results, distinct from commands, places, files, settings, web/system results or AI answers — the same gap found in the autocomplete entry's IntelliSense instance.

dims.name: Summoning
dims.q: How is the palette opened and moded?

dims.name: Arguments
dims.q: How does a command collect what it needs?

dims.name: Ranking
dims.q: Who decides which results come first?

vars.name: Pinned by the person
vars.def: The person fixes chosen commands to the top of the list; the order is authored rather than matched, learned or contextual

vars.name: Manually pinned
vars.def: The person manually pins specific commands to the top of the list, rather than the system ranking by fuzzy match, frequency/recency, selection context or predicted next action.

dims.name: Command scope
dims.q: How far does it reach?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where does it appear?

vars.name: Prompt line at the bottom edge
vars.def: The palette is a single line docked to the bottom of the window (a minibuffer or status line) rather than a floating surface

entries.name: Bottom sheet
entries.def: A surface anchored to the bottom edge that can be dragged between heights, common on phones.

dims.name: Heights
dims.q: Where can it rest?

dims.name: Modality
dims.q: Can content behind it be used?

dims.name: Contents
dims.q: What does it hold?

vars.name: Form
vars.def: Fields or option pickers ending in a confirm action (Apple Pay sheet, DoorDash item options)

vars.name: A list of results or options
vars.def: The sheet holds a set of things to choose between — ride types, routes, search results — rather than actions on one thing or the detail of one thing

vars.name: A form or transaction
vars.def: The sheet holds fields and a total to review and authorise, such as a payment sheet

vars.name: Comments or discussion thread
vars.def: A scrollable list of comments or discussion about the item behind, with a composer to add one.

vars.name: Status or tracking timeline
vars.def: A persistent status/progress timeline for an ongoing process (delivery, ride, order) shown over live map or content.

vars.name: Search input
vars.def: A search field with live suggestions, resting at a peek height and growing as the person types.

dims.name: Dismissal
dims.q: How does it leave?

entries.name: Breadcrumbs
entries.def: A trail showing the path to the current place, each step a way back.

dims.name: Trail
dims.q: What path does it show, and how is a long path shortened?

dims.name: Step interaction
dims.q: What can be done with a step?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where does the trail sit?

entries.name: Drawer
entries.def: A panel that slides in from a screen edge, holding navigation, detail, filters or an assistant beside the main content.

dims.name: Edge and relationship
dims.q: Which edge, and does it cover, push or sit beside content?

vars.name: Overlay, no scrim
vars.def: The panel lies over the content without dimming or disabling it visually (GitHub Projects item panel, Notion side peek, OS panels)

dims.name: Contents
dims.q: What is it for?

vars.name: System status and controls
vars.def: Notifications, quick toggles and widgets belonging to the OS rather than the app (Android shade, iOS Control Center, Windows Widgets, macOS Notification Center)

vars.name: Companion apps
vars.def: Small versions of other products beside the main one (Gmail's Calendar/Keep/Tasks side panel)

vars.name: Notifications and system controls
vars.def: Alerts, quick toggles and glanceable widgets belonging to the system rather than to the application underneath — notification shades, control centres, widget panels

vars.name: A companion app
vars.def: The panel runs a different application beside the current one (a calendar or notes app inside a mail client) rather than any part of the host

dims.name: Opening
dims.q: How does it open?

dims.name: Across sizes
dims.q: Does it change with the screen?

vars.name: Modal when small, docked when large

entries.name: Menu
entries.def: A transient list of choices or commands revealed from a trigger.

dims.name: Opening
dims.q: What opens it?

dims.name: Structure
dims.q: How are items organized?

dims.name: Item content
dims.q: What does each item show?

dims.name: Item set
dims.q: Who decides which items appear and in what order?

dims.name: Form
dims.q: What shape is it?

entries.name: Modal dialog
entries.def: A window over the page that holds interaction until it is dismissed, used for focused tasks, confirmations and quick detail.

dims.name: Size and position
dims.q: How big is it, and where?

vars.name: Anchored bubble
vars.def: The dialog opens attached to the element that raised it — a time slot, a cell — rather than centred, at an edge or full screen, while still holding interaction until it is answered

dims.name: Opening and closing
dims.q: What opens it, and what closes it?

vars.name: URL
vars.def: The dialog has its own address

dims.name: Modality
dims.q: What does it block?

dims.name: Contents
dims.q: What is it for?

vars.name: Selection list
vars.def: A list to choose one option from (which playlist to add to, where to share) — not a confirmation, a filled-in form, a detail view, media, or a multi-step task.

dims.name: Unsaved work
dims.q: What happens to work when it closes?

vars.name: Already saved
vars.def: Edits made inside the dialog persist as they are made, so closing discards nothing (Airtable expanded record)

entries.name: Pagination
entries.def: Dividing a long collection into portions and moving between them.

dims.name: Mechanism
dims.q: How does a person reach the next portion?

dims.name: Position
dims.q: How does a person know where they are?

vars.name: Count only
vars.def: A total number of results with previous/next, but no page number or item range (Stripe Dashboard lists)

dims.name: Page size
dims.q: How big is a portion?

dims.name: Position memory
dims.q: Is the position kept?

entries.name: Popover
entries.def: A small, non-blocking surface anchored to an element that shows detail or controls about it.

dims.name: Opening and closing
dims.q: What brings it up, and what makes it go away?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where does it sit relative to the anchor?

dims.name: Contents
dims.q: What does it hold?

dims.name: Persistence
dims.q: How long does it last?

entries.name: Stepper
entries.def: A visual trail of ordered steps showing how far a person has come and, often, letting them move between steps.

dims.name: Navigation rule
dims.q: Can a person move freely between steps?

dims.name: Form
dims.q: How is it drawn?

vars.name: Vertical list
vars.def: Steps stacked in a rail beside the content, without the content expanding under each step (Stripe activation, GOV.UK task list, macOS Installer)

dims.name: Step states
dims.q: What states can a step show?

vars.name: Not started
vars.def: A step explicitly marked as not yet begun or not yet available, distinct from merely being after the current one (GOV.UK task list tags)

vars.name: In progress
vars.def: A step is explicitly marked as started-but-not-finished, distinct from not yet started, currently active, fully completed, or in error.

dims.name: Step labels
dims.q: What does a step say?

vars.name: No labels
vars.def: The stepper shows only a progress indicator (a growing or filling bar) with no step numbers, percentages, or titles printed on it at all.

entries.name: Tabs
entries.def: A set of peer views sharing one space, one visible at a time, switched by labelled controls.

dims.name: Placement and overflow
dims.q: Where are tabs, and what happens when there are too many?

dims.name: Labels
dims.q: What does a tab say?

dims.name: Tab origin and grouping
dims.q: Who makes tabs, and can they be grouped?

vars.name: Pinned and preview tabs
vars.def: A preview tab is replaced unless kept

dims.name: Background tabs
dims.q: What happens to a tab you are not looking at?

dims.name: Switching
dims.q: How does a person switch?

entries.name: Tree view
entries.def: A hierarchical list whose nodes expand to reveal their children.

dims.name: Node content
dims.q: What does a node show?

dims.name: Expansion
dims.q: How do nodes open?

dims.name: Selection
dims.q: What can be selected?

dims.name: Hierarchy source
dims.q: What makes one node the parent of another?

dims.name: Density
dims.q: How tight is the tree?

entries.name: Plan in time
entries.def: Arrange things along time and coordinate availability with others — the activity behind calendars, booking slots, project plans and personal to-dos.

dims.name: Time representation
dims.q: How is time made visible, and at what grain?

vars.name: Continuous timeline
vars.def: A scrollable span of any length

vars.name: List of moments
vars.def: Time as ordered text, not a grid

vars.name: Zoomable span
vars.def: Pinch or scroll changes the window

vars.name: Jump to date
vars.def: Pick a date without changing scale

dims.name: Placement and conflict
dims.q: How do items sit relative to each other on time, and what happens when they overlap?

vars.name: Absolute on a calendar
vars.def: Start and end on a clock

vars.name: Relative among tasks
vars.def: Order and dependencies, not clock time

vars.name: Pinned to a day
vars.def: An item sits on a date (optionally a time) without a duration and without ordering or dependencies among items; neither Absolute on a calendar nor Relative among tasks fits a dated to-do

dims.name: Whose time
dims.q: Whose calendar or availability is in play?

vars.name: Shared calendar
vars.def: A group reads or writes one calendar

dims.name: Editing commitment
dims.q: When does placing something become binding, and how does it change later?

vars.name: Recurring series
vars.def: One edit may affect many instances

entries.name: Availability picker
entries.def: A surface for choosing a free time from offered or computed availability — for booking someone else, polling a group, or finding mutual free slots.

dims.name: How availability is defined
dims.q: What makes a slot free, and what does the booker see?

vars.name: Named conflicts for owner
vars.def: Owner sees titles; guest does not

dims.name: Choosing a slot
dims.q: What is the path from browsing times to a hold?

vars.name: Recurring series pick
vars.def: Choose a pattern, not one slot

dims.name: Slot presentation
dims.q: How are candidate times arranged?

vars.name: Options table
vars.def: Proposed options as columns and respondents as rows, each cell a yes/if-need-be/no mark

vars.name: Chips around requested time
vars.def: The guest names a target time and sees the nearest available seatings as a short row of chips, not a full day or week of slots

vars.name: Poll grid of options
vars.def: A small set of specific date/time options proposed by the organizer are laid out as a table (one column per option) for participants to mark, rather than a real calendar grid, a busy-shaded timeline, a ranked list, or a map

dims.name: Constraints and buffers
dims.q: What rules shrink the set of bookable times?

vars.name: Party size or capacity
vars.def: The number of people or seats asked for decides which slots exist at all — a table for six, a class with two spots left — a constraint on the resource rather than on the host's time

dims.name: Hold and confirm
dims.q: When is the slot reserved, and how long does a hold last?

vars.name: Poll closes later
vars.def: No hold until a winner is chosen

dims.name: Who drives
dims.q: Who proposes times — host, guest or system?

entries.name: Calendar
entries.def: A time-grid or agenda of events with start and end times, browsed by day, week or month and edited by creating, dragging or inviting.

dims.name: Event content
dims.q: What does each event show on the grid versus in detail?

dims.name: View structure
dims.q: How is the span of time laid out?

dims.name: Creating and moving
dims.q: How are events created, opened and repositioned?

vars.name: From email or chat
vars.def: Offer to add a detected time

dims.name: Coordination
dims.q: How do invites, responses and shared visibility work?

dims.name: Working context
dims.q: How does the calendar adapt to working hours, timezone and device?

dims.name: Density and span
dims.q: Which events are in the current view, and how crowded is it?

entries.name: Gantt timeline
entries.def: Tasks or phases as bars on a horizontal time axis, often with dependencies, progress and a hierarchical work breakdown beside the bars.

dims.name: Bar and row content
dims.q: What does each bar and row say about the work?

dims.name: Dependencies and constraints
dims.q: How are tasks linked, and what may move freely?

dims.name: Timeline layout
dims.q: How are axis scale and panes arranged?

dims.name: Editing bars
dims.q: How are start, end and links changed?

dims.name: Planning vs tracking
dims.q: How does the timeline show plan quality and slippage?

dims.name: Whose plan
dims.q: Who can edit, and how are parallel plans reconciled?

entries.name: Task list
entries.def: Ordered or grouped actionable items with completion state, often carrying due dates, assignees and priority without requiring a full time grid.

dims.name: Task representation
dims.q: What does each row show, and how rich is the item?

dims.name: Ordering and grouping
dims.q: What structure holds the tasks?

dims.name: Scheduling link
dims.q: How does the list connect to clock time?

vars.name: Time block on calendar
vars.def: Task appears as a calendar event

dims.name: Completing and triaging
dims.q: How do tasks move toward done or deferral?

vars.name: Snooze / defer
vars.def: Leave incomplete but hide until later

dims.name: Creation and detail
dims.q: How are tasks added and opened?

vars.name: Save from elsewhere
vars.def: Items enter the list by being captured from another surface — starring an email, saving a message, syncing an issue from another tool — rather than being typed into the list at all

dims.name: Personal vs shared
dims.q: Whose list is it, and how is assignment shared?

entries.name: Search and discover
entries.def: Express what you want and get candidates back, or be shown what you might want before you ask.

dims.name: Query form
dims.q: In what form is intent expressed?

dims.name: Who initiates
dims.q: Does the person pull, or does the system push?

dims.name: Result form
dims.q: In what form do candidates come back?

vars.name: In-place highlights
vars.def: Matches are marked where they already sit (on the page) with a count and next/previous stepping, rather than returned as a list

vars.name: Matches in place
vars.def: There is no result list: the matches are marked in the content itself and navigated one at a time, with a count for orientation (find in page, find in a document or code editor)

dims.name: Refinement
dims.q: How does the search move forward after the first results?

dims.name: Index scope
dims.q: What is searched?

entries.name: Faceted search
entries.def: Search combined with attribute facets whose values and counts update as the result set narrows.

dims.name: Facet content
dims.q: Which facet types are offered, and how are values shown?

dims.name: Facet set
dims.q: Where does the set of facets come from?

vars.name: Added by the person
vars.def: Any attribute can become a facet

dims.name: Update model
dims.q: When does a facet change take effect?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where do facets live?

vars.name: Modal dialog
vars.def: Facets live in a centred dialog over the results on desktop web

dims.name: Selection logic
dims.q: How do chosen values combine?

dims.name: Visual facets
dims.q: Are facets drawn, not just listed?

entries.name: Recommendations
entries.def: Items proposed by the system from a person’s behaviour, context or the current item, rather than from a query.

dims.name: Basis
dims.q: On what grounds is something recommended?

dims.name: Rationale
dims.q: Does the recommendation say why?

dims.name: Placement
dims.q: Where do recommendations appear?

vars.name: Dedicated queue
vars.def: A surface whose only content is recommendations, presented one at a time and advanced deliberately (Steam's Discovery Queue, swipe-to-decide apps) — not a shelf inside another screen, not an up-next after content and not a periodic digest

dims.name: Steering controls
dims.q: How can a person steer?

dims.name: Freshness
dims.q: How often do recommendations change?

dims.name: Nesting
dims.q: How are shelves composed?

entries.name: Search results
entries.def: A ranked presentation of items matching a query, with the cues needed to judge relevance and the tools to refine.

dims.name: Result representation
dims.q: What does a result show, and how is its snippet made?

dims.name: Grouping
dims.q: Is it one list or many?

vars.name: Blended modules
vars.def: Videos, maps and stories in one list

vars.name: Grouped by type
vars.def: Results are sectioned by the kind of thing they are (songs, artists, playlists; applications, documents, mail) in one scroll, rather than split into tabs, blended into a single list or clustered by subject. The archetype entry has this value; this entry does not

dims.name: Ranking control
dims.q: How much say does the person have in the order?

dims.name: Relevance cues
dims.q: What helps a person judge a result before opening it?

vars.name: Rating and popularity
vars.def: The judging signal is a crowd aggregate carried on the result — star rating and review count, downloads, citations, views — which in app, product and scholarly search decides more clicks than the snippet does

dims.name: Result preview
dims.q: Where does a result open?

dims.name: Updating
dims.q: When do results change?

entries.name: Transact and commit
entries.def: Make a consequential choice, commit to it, and be able to take it back.

dims.name: Commit structure
dims.q: How many steps stand between choosing and committing?

dims.name: Consequence disclosure
dims.q: What is said about consequences before committing?

dims.name: Reversal
dims.q: How can it be taken back?

dims.name: Defaults and nudges
dims.q: How does the system shape the choice?

vars.name: Scarcity pressure
vars.def: The choice is shaped by manufactured urgency rather than by a recommendation — only 2 left at this price, 12 other people are looking, this deal ends in 9 minutes

dims.name: Unit
dims.q: What is being committed to?

entries.name: Approval flow
entries.def: Routing a request to people who approve it, reject it or ask for changes.

dims.name: Routing
dims.q: Who reviews, in what order?

dims.name: Review surface
dims.q: What does a reviewer see?

dims.name: Decision actions
dims.q: How is a decision made?

dims.name: Timing
dims.q: What if nobody decides?

dims.name: Visibility
dims.q: Who sees the discussion and history?

dims.name: Status to requester
dims.q: What does the requester see while waiting?

entries.name: Booking flow
entries.def: Choosing a time, place or seat from what is available, then reserving it.

dims.name: Selection order
dims.q: In what order are choices made?

dims.name: Availability
dims.q: How is what can be booked shown?

dims.name: Hold
dims.q: Is the choice held while deciding?

dims.name: Price and scarcity
dims.q: How are price and scarcity signalled?

dims.name: Party and extras
dims.q: What else is booked with it?

dims.name: Confirmation
dims.q: How is the booking confirmed?

entries.name: Checkout
entries.def: The flow that turns a cart into a paid order: contact, delivery, payment and review.

dims.name: Structure
dims.q: How is the flow divided?

dims.name: Order summary
dims.q: How visible is what is being bought?

dims.name: Prefill
dims.q: What arrives filled in?

dims.name: Cost disclosure
dims.q: When is the full cost known?

dims.name: Payment options
dims.q: How are ways to pay offered?

dims.name: Abandonment
dims.q: What happens when a person leaves?

entries.name: Plan picker
entries.def: Presenting tiers of a product or subscription to choose among.

dims.name: Presentation
dims.q: How are tiers arranged?

vars.name: Stacked list
vars.def: Tiers as a vertical list of rows with a radio or tap target, one line each, with no side-by-side columns or feature table (mobile upgrade sheets)

dims.name: Feature disclosure
dims.q: How are features compared?

dims.name: Recommendation
dims.q: Does the page steer?

dims.name: Price framing
dims.q: How is price expressed?

dims.name: Commitment
dims.q: What does choosing commit to?

entries.name: Confirmation
entries.def: A deliberate pause asking a person to confirm a consequential action.

dims.name: Friction
dims.q: How much effort does confirming take?

vars.name: Swipe to confirm
vars.def: A slider or swipe gesture commits the action, so it cannot be triggered by a stray tap

vars.name: Physical button plus biometric
vars.def: A hardware button press (double-click the side button) combined with Face ID or Touch ID authorises the action

vars.name: Biometric confirm
vars.def: Confirming means authenticating — Face ID, a fingerprint, a hardware button press — rather than pressing a button in the interface; the proof of intent comes from the device

vars.name: Re-authenticate
vars.def: Confirming requires proving who you are again — re-entering the password or a 2FA code — rather than typing the object's name

dims.name: Explanation
dims.q: What does it explain?

dims.name: When to ask
dims.q: Under what conditions does it appear?

vars.name: On a likely mistake
vars.def: The dialog appears only when a heuristic suggests a slip (empty subject, 'attached' with no attachment), not on every action or only irreversible ones

vars.name: On a detected condition
vars.def: The dialog appears only because the system noticed something specific about this particular action (an empty subject line, unsaved changes, a mentioned attachment that is missing) — not because the action is always dangerous

dims.name: Form
dims.q: Where does it ask?

entries.name: Undo
entries.def: Reversing recent actions.

dims.name: Unit
dims.q: What can be undone?

dims.name: Access
dims.q: How is it triggered?

vars.name: Multi-finger gesture
vars.def: A touch gesture such as a two-finger tap or three-finger swipe triggers undo, distinct from shaking the device

vars.name: Context menu on the item
vars.def: Undo is offered in the long-press or right-click menu of the thing just acted on, not globally

vars.name: Touch gesture
vars.def: A multi-finger tap or swipe on the canvas or page undoes, with no button, shortcut or toast involved (Procreate's two-finger tap, iOS three-finger swipe)

vars.name: Context menu on the object
vars.def: Undo is reached by long-pressing or right-clicking the affected object itself — the sent message, the moved file — rather than from any global undo control

dims.name: Window
dims.q: How long is undo possible?

dims.name: Multiple people
dims.q: Whose actions are undone?

dims.name: Preview
dims.q: Does it say what will be undone?
